chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came to Abu al-Abbas while he was at al-Hira, one day he went out intending (to meet) Isa ibn Musa. He met him between al-Hira and al-Kufa, and with him was Ibn Shubruma, the judge. He said to him (the Imam): 'Where are you going, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'I intended (to meet) you.' He said: 'Allah has shortened your steps.' He said: So he went along with him.

Then Ibn Shubruma said to him (the Imam): 'What do you say, O Abu Abdillah, regarding something which the Emir asked me about, but I had nothing to say about it?' He said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'He asked me about the first letter/document written on earth.'

He (the Imam) said: 'Yes. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, presented to Adam (peace be upon him) his offspring to his eyes, in the form of particles — prophet after prophet, king after king, believer after believer, and disbeliever after disbeliever. When He reached David (peace be upon him), he (Adam) said: Who is this whom You have granted prophethood, honoured him, yet shortened his lifespan?'

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'This is your son David; his age is forty years, and I have indeed written the lifespans, distributed the provisions, and I obliterate what I will and affirm (what I will), and with Me is the Mother of the Book. So if you make something of your lifespan for him, I shall attach it to him.' He (Adam) said: 'O Lord! I have made sixty years from my lifespan for him, to complete one hundred.'

He (the narrator) said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Jibrail, Mika'il and the Angel of Death: 'Write upon him a document, for he will indeed forget.' He said: So they wrote a document upon him (Adam) and sealed it with their wings from the clay of Illiyeen.

He said: So when death presented itself to Adam, the Angel of Death came to him. Adam said: 'O Angel of Death! What has brought you?' He said: 'I have come to seize your soul.' He said: 'But sixty years remain of my lifespan.' He (the Angel of Death) said: 'You made it for your son David.' He (the narrator) said: And Jibrail descended upon him and brought out the document.
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: For that reason, when the promissory note (sakk) is produced against the debtor, the debtor is humbled. Thus he (the Angel) seized his (Adam's) soul.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab) — the primordial divine record from which destinies are recorded and can be altered
key_terms.الصَّكّ: Sakk (promissory note / legal document) — the first such binding written covenant, originating in the divine record of Adam's pledge
key_terms.عِلِّيُّون: Illiyeen — the highest celestial realm, from which clay was used to seal the divine covenant

ai.seo_question: What was the first document ever written on earth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narrative, reported by Abdullah ibn Sinan, recounts Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) encounter with Ibn Shubruma, a judge who served the Abbasid court, at al-Hira. Ibn Shubruma had been stumped by a question from the Emir about the first document written on earth, so he posed it to the Imam. In response, the Imam narrated the cosmic event of Adam witnessing his offspring before creation, interceding for his son David's short lifespan by gifting him sixty years — a covenant written by angels and sealed in clay from Illiyeen. The Imam then draws a jurisprudential analogy: just as Adam was humbled when his covenant/document was produced against him at his death, so too is a debtor humbled when a promissory note (sakk) is issued against them, explaining the spiritual origin of binding legal documents.
